title: QUIC Connection Migration Hosted Proof Lane Verification
verification_method: Requirement-home tests, helper dry-run planning, workflow review, artifact inspection, and hosted workflow dispatch when external evidence is required.
preconditions: The external `quic-interop-runner` checkout includes `ngtcp2`, `quiche`, `aioquic`, `picoquic`, `lsquic`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, `quinn`, and `neqo` peer slots.
Hosted dispatch has Docker Engine 28.1 or later, Python 3.12, and Wireshark packet-analysis tools available.
The repo-local helper remains responsible for image replacement, runner invocation, inventory output, and per-cell artifact capture.
scope: Verify that the repository exposes manual advisory hosted proof lanes for server-role connectionmigration against neqo using a distinct local nginx replacement slot, the neqo-peer helper alias, the normalized neqo runner peer slot, and the OCI-indexed neqo-qns image, plus a blocked comparison lane for ngtcp2, lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic, without promoting blocked cells or changing ordinary CI gates. The current proof also verifies that the harness keeps the configured preferred migration address reachable without letting it become the original-path first-flight source address.
procedure: Review `.github/workflows/interop-runner-handshake.yml` and confirm the `connectionmigration-server-proof` and `connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` profiles are `workflow_dispatch` only.

Confirm the proof profile includes a server-role matrix cell that replaces the local `nginx` slot, records `neqo-peer` as the peer alias, and invokes the runner against the normalized `neqo` client slot for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm the blocked profile includes server-role matrix cells against `ngtcp2`, `lsquic`, `quiche`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `aioquic` for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm every matrix cell invokes `scripts/interop/Invoke-QuicInteropRunner.ps1` with matrix-provided role, local implementation slot, peer slot, testcase, timeout, and artifact root.
Confirm each cell uploads a distinct artifact bundle with `if: always()`.
Run the focused requirement-home tests for `REQ-QUIC-INT-0018` and `REQ-QUIC-INT-0022`.
Run the captured neqo connectionmigration qlog replay in `REQ-QUIC-CRT-0112` to prove the hosted server first flight opens with the published Initial and Handshake secrets.
Run representative helper dry-run plans for the server-role neqo connectionmigration cell using the local `nginx` replacement slot, plus the blocked comparison peers.

When external evidence is required, dispatch `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof` and `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` and inspect each uploaded `runner-report.json` plus selected output logs.
expected_result: The repository configuration provides opt-in hosted proof lanes that can collect per-cell artifacts for Incursa.Quic as the server role against neqo using a distinct local nginx replacement slot, the neqo-peer helper alias, the normalized neqo runner peer slot, and the OCI-indexed neqo-qns image for the connectionmigration proof cells, while keeping a blocked comparison lane for ngtcp2, lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic, and keeping the major-peer-matrix profile and HTTP/3 out of scope.
status_summary: Planned/open for hosted execution, with local clean-runner proof now passing. The repository has split connectionmigration proof lanes and the helper inventory classifies connectionmigration as supported/executed. Hosted run `25864019585` cleared the alias lookup failure but exposed a replacement-slot collision because the runner invoked `-s neqo -c neqo -r neqo=incursa-quic-interop-harness:local`; the later single-path failure is therefore not accepted as a real neqo-peer migration verdict. The proof lane now uses a distinct local `nginx` replacement slot while preserving `neqo-peer` for helper reporting and normalizing the actual runner peer slot to `neqo`. Hosted runs `25866825495` and `25867235353` confirm that runner shape (`-s nginx -c neqo -r nginx=incursa-quic-interop-harness:local`), but failed before transfer or migration with server-side `TLS alert 50`. Hosted run `25868496912` moved past that failure, then exposed the earlier source-address failure. Local clean-runner proof `.artifacts/interop-runner/connectionmigration-shim-proof/20260519-163904754-server-nginx` now passed `connectionmigration` against `neqo`; the pcap starts with server packets from original address `fd00:cafe:cafe:100::100`, later observes preferred path `fd00:cafe:cafe:100::110`, and `runner-report.json` records `result: succeeded`. The repo-owned runner shim carries the analyzer compatibility needed to reproduce that proof without dirty upstream runner files. Hosted corroboration still needs a fresh manual run before hosted readiness is claimed.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Coverage
supplemental_sections.content: `http3` remains out of scope. `v2`, `rebind-port`, and `rebind-addr` remain prerequisite-blocked under the non-HTTP/3 inventory. `connectionmigration` has hosted proof lanes against neqo using a distinct local `nginx` replacement slot plus a blocked comparison lane against ngtcp2, lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic. Hosted run `25864019585` is retained only as collision evidence because it replaced the normalized `neqo` slot on both sides. Hosted runs `25866825495` and `25867235353` prove the distinct-slot runner invocation but failed before transfer or migration with server-side `TLS alert 50`. Hosted run `25868496912` proves the server first flight is cryptographically usable but exposed the earlier preferred-address source-selection blocker. Local clean-runner proof and hosted run `26174181713` now close the bounded `connectionmigration` proof lane, while the blocked comparison lane remains advisory.
